motivation: In 2007 Lorimer, McLaughlin and Bailes found a bright, millisecond-duration radio burst in archival Parkes pulsar-survey data. Its dispersion measure placed it far beyond the Milky Way. This 'Lorimer burst' revealed an entirely new class of astrophysical phenomenon. Their dispersion-searching methods, and Bailes's later work with the HTRU survey, established fast radio bursts as a real, all-sky population. Fast radio bursts are now detected by the thousands. They have been localized to host galaxies, linked to a Galactic magnetar, and used to weigh the 'missing' cosmic baryons along their sightlines, measuring the intergalactic medium directly. The discovery opened a new window on extreme neutron-star physics, coherent emission, and cosmology. Few observations of the past two decades have created a new field so rapidly or given physics such a broadly useful probe.
